note: Plain-language stops for the Hardware options spectrum. Specs come from portfolio.json; this file adds the words. Needs: ble, zigbee, thread, matter, two_radios, ai, memory (64 kB RAM or more).

stops.name: MSP-EXP430FR2433
stops.plain: A light or a sensor that sleeps most of the day.
adds: FRAM memory: keeps data with no power
stops.line: FRAM keeps its data with no power. For a light or a sensor that sleeps most of the day.

stops.name: LP-MSPM0C1104
stops.plain: Blink a light, read a button or a simple sensor. Too small for Zephyr.
adds: Debug probe built into the board
stops.line: The smallest Arm board here. Blink a light, read a button or a simple sensor; too small for Zephyr.

stops.name: LP-MSPM0L1306
stops.step: Adds analog parts and room to grow
stops.plain: Read light, temperature and small signals with the amplifiers on the chip; small programs, even a tiny AI model.
adds: 4 times the flash (64 kB) and RAM (4 kB)
Two op-amps and a comparator; a light sensor and a thermistor on the board
drops: Still only 4 kB of RAM: Zephyr fits only when trimmed
No Zephyr board upstream; a port runs it
stops.line: The step up from the C1104 for analog: two op-amps and a comparator on the chip, a light sensor and a thermistor on the board. Room for a tiny AI model.

stops.name: LP-MSPM0L2228
stops.plain: Show numbers on the small LCD glass on the board, like a meter, and keep a clock running from a super capacitor.
adds: 8 times the RAM (32 kB) and 4 times the flash (256 kB) of the L1306
Segment LCD glass on the board, driven by the chip
A battery island: real-time clock, tamper pins and a 100 mF super capacitor on the board
AES and a true random number generator
drops: Still 32 MHz, no FPU and no math accelerator
Zephyr has the board upstream; not run here yet
stops.line: The step up from the L1306 for a meter or a clock: a segment LCD on the board, a battery-backed island with a super capacitor, and enough RAM for Zephyr.

stops.name: LP-MSPM0G3507
stops.plain: Small control and sensing projects, Zephyr, and small AI models run in software.
adds: Math accelerator, CAN bus, more analog inputs
stops.line: The step up when the L1306 runs out of memory: screens, small AI models and Zephyr. A math accelerator roughly doubles the speed of control maths.

stops.name: LP-MSPM0G3519
stops.plain: Bigger programs and more things plugged in at once.
adds: 4 times the RAM (128 kB) and flash (512 kB)
More connections: 7 serial ports, 2 CAN buses
Two flash banks, for safer firmware updates
stops.line: The step up from the G3507 for bigger programs and more things plugged in: more serial ports, two CAN buses and two flash banks for safer updates.

stops.name: LP-MSPM0G5187
stops.plain: Hear a sound or spot a pattern on the chip itself.
adds: AI accelerator for small neural networks
USB and audio; a microphone on the board
drops: Back to 32 kB RAM and 128 kB flash
stops.line: The G3507's memory with an AI accelerator and a microphone on the board. Hear a sound or spot a pattern on the chip itself.

stops.name: LP-EM-CC2340R5
stops.plain: Wireless sensors, buttons and lights, one radio at a time.
adds: A 2.4 GHz radio: Bluetooth and Zigbee
drops: 36 kB RAM, and the radio software uses most of it
stops.line: Bluetooth and Zigbee, one radio at a time, for wireless sensors, buttons and lights. The radio software uses most of the RAM.

stops.name: LP-EM-CC2340R53
stops.step: Same radio, almost twice the RAM
stops.plain: The kit TI sells now, with almost twice the RAM.
adds: Almost twice the RAM: 64 kB against 36 kB
Thread as a full device (evaluation status in the SDK release notes)
stops.line: The CC2340R5 with more RAM, and the kit TI sells now.

stops.name: LP-EM-CC2755P10
stops.plain: Room for big wireless apps and the newer smart-home standards.
adds: Matter over Thread (evaluation status in the SDK release notes)
Two radios at once: Bluetooth with Thread or TI 15.4
stops.line: Room for large wireless apps: Matter over Thread, Bluetooth with Thread at the same time, and a stronger radio.

stops.name: LAUNCHXL-CC3235SF
stops.plain: Send data to your home network with one board and one cable.
adds: Zephyr has a Wi-Fi driver for it
stops.line: Wi-Fi on one board and one cable, for sending data to your home network. No Bluetooth.

stops.name: LP-EM-CC35X1
stops.plain: A smart-home device that joins Wi-Fi with no extra hub.
stops.line: Wi-Fi 6 with Bluetooth and Matter over Wi-Fi: a smart-home device that joins your network with no hub.

stops.name: LP-CC1354P10-1
stops.plain: Sensors far from the house, past where 2.4 GHz reaches.
drops: TI's kit: debug probe sold separately
stops.line: Adds Sub-1 GHz for sensors far from the house, with room for Zigbee, Thread and Bluetooth.

stops.name: LP-CC1352P7-1
stops.plain: Long range, with the probe built in.
drops: Zephyr lists no Bluetooth for it
stops.line: Long range with the debugger on the board and Zephyr support. Less RAM than the CC1354P10.

stops.name: IWR6843AOPEVM
stops.plain: Sense people in a room without a camera.
adds: Visualizer runs in a browser on a Mac
stops.line: 60 GHz radar that senses people in a room without a camera. The visualizer runs in a browser on a Mac.

stops.name: IWRL6432AOPEVM
stops.plain: Presence sensing on less power.
drops: Tools for Windows and Linux only
stops.line: Radar for presence sensing on less power, with the debugger on the board. The tools run on Windows and Linux only.

stops.name: IWRL6432BOOST
stops.plain: Presence sensing on less power, with measured range.
adds: Held a seated person at 4 m, no false flag in 6 h
drops: Tools for Windows and Linux only
stops.line: Radar for presence sensing on less power, with the debugger on the board. It held a seated person at 4 m, the farthest distance tested, and raised no flag for the first 6 h overnight in a quiet room; the first flag came after about 6 h and was not checked against a person. The tools run on Windows and Linux only.

stops.name: LAUNCHXL-F2800137
stops.plain: Spin a motor or run a power supply, with sine and divide done in a few cycles.
adds: 120 MHz control core with trig and divide hardware (TMU)
drops: Not Arm: new tools to learn
stops.line: A control chip, not Arm: trig and divide in hardware, for spinning a motor or running a power supply.

stops.name: LAUNCHXL-F28P55X
stops.plain: Spin a motor smoothly and precisely.
drops: Not Arm: new tools to learn
stops.line: The step up from the F2800137 for motor control: a faster core, more PWM outputs and three encoder inputs.

stops.name: LP-AM263P
stops.plain: Four fast real-time cores, lots of on-chip RAM and PWM for motor and power control, with two Ethernet ports on the board.
adds: Two Gigabit Ethernet ports on the board
drops: Needs a 5 V, 3 A USB-C supply
stops.line: Four 400 MHz real-time cores with 3 MB of on-chip RAM, for motor and power control that outgrows one core.

stops.name: PocketBeagle 2
stops.plain: A tiny Linux computer for Python and scripts.
stops.zephyr_note: Zephyr runs on its Cortex-M4F core, not on the Linux cores
stops.line: A tiny Linux computer for Python and scripts. No radio.

stops.name: BeaglePlay
stops.step: Linux with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee and Sub-1 GHz
stops.plain: A home hub: Linux, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee and Sub-1 GHz.
stops.zephyr_note: Zephyr runs on its Cortex-M4F core (target beagleplay/am6254/m4) or its CC1352P7 radio chip (beagleplay/cc1352p7), not on the Linux cores
stops.line: A home hub running Linux, with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee and Sub-1 GHz, HDMI and Ethernet.

stops.name: TMDS62LEVM
stops.step: Linux on one core, real-time Zephyr on the other
stops.plain: A low-power Linux processor whose second core can run Zephyr as the real-time coprocessor, talking to Linux through shared memory.
adds: 2 GB LPDDR4 and 32 GB eMMC on the board
drops: Needs a 5 V to 15 V, 3 A USB-C supply
stops.line: Linux on one A53 core and Zephyr on the other, exchanging messages through shared DDR in about 6 microseconds.

stops.name: SK-TDA4VM
stops.plain: A Linux computer with a deep-learning accelerator and video codecs, for camera and vision projects.
stops.line: A Linux computer with a deep-learning accelerator and video codecs, for camera and vision projects.

lanes.name: No radio: small chips
lanes.sub: Each step adds speed, memory, connections or a special part.

lanes.name: Bluetooth, Zigbee and Thread
lanes.sub: Adds a 2.4 GHz radio, then more memory for bigger wireless software.

lanes.name: Wi-Fi
lanes.sub: Joins your home network directly, no hub needed.

lanes.name: Long range
lanes.sub: Adds Sub-1 GHz, which reaches farther than 2.4 GHz, for sensors far from the house.

lanes.name: Special jobs: radar and motors
lanes.sub: Chips built for one job: sensing people with radar, or spinning a motor smoothly.

lanes.name: Runs Linux
lanes.sub: A small computer, not a microcontroller. Made by BeagleBoard.org around TI chips; not sold on TI.com.
